note.question: Can combining an externality score with an ordinary product-quality rating make all consumers discipline producers to reduce external harms?
note.overview: A long-lived strategic producer repeatedly chooses investments in product quality and externality reduction before short-lived consumers observe rating histories and choose whether to buy. The paper derives reputation equilibria and tests their predictions experimentally.

components.label: Repeated-game reputation equilibrium with full producer investment
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Repeated-game reputation equilibrium with full producer investment. Proposition 1 states the thresholds for a full-investment equilibrium: with separate ratings it exists if and only if lambda is at least c_DR/(delta p), whereas under a combined rating it may exist for any lambda and always exists once lambda reaches max{c_PQ,c_DR}/(delta p). The appendix supplies formal beliefs and proofs, and the text discusses additional equilibria.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: In each period, the producer chooses whether to invest in product quality and whether to reduce external damage. A newly matched consumer observes the available rating history, updates beliefs, and decides whether to purchase at a fixed price. Payoffs realize and the investment outcomes enter future average ratings; the interaction repeats with a discounted strategic producer. Separate ratings let consumers punish only the attribute they care about, so regular consumers do not discipline damage reduction.
